quoted.text:
Adrian Peterson says he chose Oklahoma over Texas after Mack Brown told him he would redshirt behind Cedric Benson despite being the No. 1 recruit in the country

“Me being from Texas, I was a Longhorn all the way. My uncle went there, so I used to go to the games. He played with Ricky Williams, [Major] Applewhite, and Priest Holmes. I was seeing guys run the rock. So that that really had me locked in even more”

“But ultimately what it came down to it was Cedric Benson had decided to come back for his senior year. He was projected to be a top five pick his junior year. Stayed there, decided to come back to Texas. So, Mack Brown was like, ‘Hey, man, we gonna be loyal to Cedric because he’s coming back, and pretty much we’re going to redshirt’”

“I’m the number one player in the country. I got USC, they got Reggie Bush, LenDale White and Hershel Dennis. They telling me if I come in, I can compete for the spot. Every school was telling me the same thing but Texas. That really shifted my focus. So it really came down between USC and Oklahoma”

text:
AI models are trained on everything, including torture, lying, hacking, biological weapons and Charles Manson.

No one knows if it’s possible to create a remarkably intelligent, relentless AI model that at its core is not depraved.

This is why we need to pass AI Kill Switch Act. https://t.co/BjXgzlTSd5

quoted.text:
Alexandr Wang ( @alexandr_wang, Chief AI Officer at Meta): nobody knows how to solve alignment yet

"This is, I think, one of the most open questions scientifically in AI. I think nobody knows exactly the way to solve this problem, but there’s a few ideas."

His solution is "scalable oversight": 

“as the AIs get smarter, we use a different set of AIs to observe what they’re doing and keep them in check.” 

The watcher AIs have to improve along with the models they watch, so labs would need to build “smarter and smarter policing agents” too. 

Meta’s Muse already uses a version of this, with a separate sentinel agent checking what the main agent does.

----  
Full video on "Cleo Abram" YouTube channel, (link in comment)
